memory_update.text: Highest-priority Energy chokepoint is grid deliverability, especially large power transformers, distribution transformers, substations, switchgear, and transmission interconnection rather than generic electricity demand alone.

AI/data-center load is the dominant demand driver to track, but Serenity mapping should also include industrial manufacturing load, LNG/gas demand, electrification, and local permitting as interacting drivers.
Track PJM/FERC large-load, co-location, price-collar, expedited interconnection, and backstop procurement actions as near-term regulatory catalysts.
Track earnings disclosures from electrical-equipment and gas-turbine suppliers for backlog, book-to-bill, lead times, data-center order mix, and capacity-expansion plans.

Next layer should verify company-specific exposure for Layer 1 candidates: data-center/grid revenue mix, backlog quality, customer concentration, margin durability, capacity additions, and whether current valuation already prices the bottleneck.
Need region-by-region validation for ERCOT, PJM, SERC/Southeast, WECC, and MISO because load growth, market design, interconnection rules, fuel constraints, and rate treatment differ materially.

POWL is a direct electrical-equipment chokepoint candidate for AI/data-center power delivery via engineered switchgear, control, and distribution systems; evidence is strong on backlog but needs end-market mix and lead-time validation.

HUBB is a utility-grid infrastructure supplier mapped to T&D, substation, grid hardening, and electrical-solutions demand; relationship strength depends on utility capex and substation order evidence.

FIX is a high-quality mission-critical construction execution candidate because backlog growth and company disclosures point to strong technology/data-center demand, including modular and electrical operations.
STRL maps to data-center site development and E-Infrastructure rather than equipment scarcity; verify data-center concentration and acquired electrical/mechanical revenue contribution.
EME maps to electrical and mechanical construction labor/execution for data centers and network/communications projects; must separate organic demand from Miller Electric acquisition contribution.
IESC maps to specialized electrical and communications installation for data centers, with record Communications backlog and favorable large data-center project execution disclosed in fiscal 2025.

D is a regulated-utility expression of Northern Virginia/PJM DOM data-center load growth; upside and risk depend heavily on Virginia SCC rate treatment, large-load tariffs, IRP approvals, and bill backlash.
NVT is a component-level data-center and utility infrastructure supplier; current evidence supports exposure but not yet hard bottleneck control.

VST is a firm-power scarcity candidate through nuclear and gas generation in constrained power markets, with a material Meta PPA disclosed for PJM nuclear output; relationship remains sensitive to market rules, hedging, and regulatory outcomes.

EQIX and DLR are demand-side data-center platforms; they validate the load-growth theme but may be beneficiaries or cost bearers depending on power procurement, lease pricing, capex inflation, and interconnection access.

CMI maps directly to backup and on-site data-center power through generators, controls, paralleling systems, transfer switches, and generator technologies; emissions rules and competition are key falsification vectors.

Need market-pricing layer before any ranking upgrade: valuation, revenue exposure, backlog quality, margin normalization, order conversion, customer concentration, capex needs, balance sheet pressure, and crowding/short-interest checks for all tickers.
Need primary-source filings for NVT with explicit data-center and power-utility revenue mix; current relationship evidence is less specific than for POWL, FIX, CMI, EME, IESC, and STRL.

Need regional mapping between PJM, ERCOT, Virginia, Texas, Georgia, Pennsylvania, and other data-center hot spots to distinguish utilities, contractors, and suppliers with local exposure from generic electrification beta.

ETN should be tracked as a broad electrical-equipment/data-center power distribution beneficiary; key Serenity evidence variables are Electrical backlog, book-to-bill, data-center order mix, lead times, and margin expansion.
PWR is one of the cleanest public mappings to the grid EPC and skilled-labor bottleneck; 2025 record total backlog and Electric segment backlog support upgrading evidence quality.
GEV spans dispatchable generation equipment and grid equipment; gas turbine slot reservations and grid-product order growth are the main Layer 3 validation fields.
CEG has direct evidence for hyperscaler nuclear demand through the Microsoft 20-year Crane Clean Energy Center PPA; key risk is restart/regulatory/capex execution rather than thematic relevance.
LEU is the most direct public-market mapping in this chunk to the HALEU bottleneck, but contract/task-order funding and production scale remain the key falsification variables.
CCJ maps to uranium, UF6 conversion, fuel services, and Westinghouse; evidence is strong for nuclear fuel-cycle exposure but less direct for AI/data-center power demand.
SO has concrete Southeast load-growth evidence tied to data centers and advanced manufacturing; economics should be validated through IRPs, rate cases, and large-load contract structures.
PCG has data-center load evidence but should be kept in a regulatory-risk bucket because wildfire liabilities, affordability, and CPUC cost recovery can dominate the load-growth thesis.
NEE and AES are renewables/storage PPA mappings; Serenity priority should depend on interconnection-ready contracted backlog and data-center customer exposure, not broad renewables exposure.

Need a current Layer 3 market-pricing check for all names: valuation versus normalized earnings, backlog-to-revenue conversion, crowding, short interest, customer concentration, and whether AI-power exposure is already priced in.
Need company-level 2026 updates for all tickers because the Energy/data-center power theme is moving quickly and backlog, capacity, contract, and regulatory facts may change quarter to quarter.

Within the LNG/midstream part of the candidate chunk, WMB and ET have the clearest data-center/power-demand relationships because they disclose specific data-center or power-plant gas capacity projects and long-duration demand-pull contracts.
KMI is relevant to data-center power demand through gas-pipeline infrastructure but currently needs more customer/project-level evidence than WMB and ET before being upgraded in the Serenity funnel.

LNG is a global LNG export and gas-demand proxy, not a direct AI data-center power-delivery chokepoint; monitor whether U.S. domestic gas demand tightens feedgas costs or improves LNG contracting power.
FSLR has credible domestic solar manufacturing/backlog exposure, but the Serenity chokepoint remains downstream interconnection, transmission, storage, and firm capacity rather than modules alone.
FLNC maps to a plausible grid-flexibility chokepoint, but backlog-to-margin conversion and battery supply-chain risk are the decisive next validation points.

ENPH is lower priority for the AI/data-center power chokepoint because current evidence is dominated by residential solar cyclicality and U.S. policy headwinds; upgrade only if grid-edge/VPP or commercial storage evidence becomes material.
FCX and SCCO should be treated as broad copper commodity proxies for grid/electrification capex; Serenity validation requires copper market-pricing, supply-cost, and jurisdictional risk checks.
MP is strategically relevant to domestic rare earth magnets but is less direct to the immediate grid/data-center power chokepoint than natural-gas delivery, transformers, switchgear, and storage.

Need comparable valuation/crowding check across WMB, ET, KMI, LNG, FSLR, ENPH, FLNC, FCX, SCCO, and MP before any Layer 3 prioritization; this layer maps relationships only and does not make buy/sell recommendations.

Need standardized company-level metrics: percentage of EBITDA/revenue tied to target node, backlog/book-to-bill, contract duration, capex remaining, in-service schedule, regulatory risk, and margin sensitivity.

summary: Split Layer 2 synthesis. Initial Layer 2A industry-chain map for the Energy theme, framed around the current U.S. power-system chokepoint: electricity demand is re-accelerating after years of flat load, with AI/data centers, manufacturing, electrification, LNG/gas-power demand, and grid reliability needs pulling on the same scarce nodes. The highest-bottleneck nodes are not generic energy commodities alone; they are grid interconnection, transformers, switchgear/substations, dispatchable generation availability, gas-turbine slots, utility transmission and distribution execution, and regulatory cost-allocation rules.

supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Large, power-dense campuses convert compute capex into electricity demand, interconnection requests, backup-power needs, water/permitting scrutiny, and local grid upgrades. This is the primary incremental demand shock behind the Serenity energy funnel.

Semiconductors, batteries, reshoring, LNG, hydrogen, and electrified industrial processes add non-data-center load that competes for the same generation, transformers, substations, interconnection studies, and EPC labor.

supply_chain_map.node: Utility load forecasting and interconnection queue
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Forecast accuracy determines how much transmission, generation, and capacity-market procurement is planned. Underforecasting delays infrastructure; overforecasting risks stranded capex and ratepayer backlash.

Even when generation exists, new large loads cannot be energized without transmission capacity, network upgrades, studies, and deliverability approvals. This is a system-level chokepoint with multi-year timelines.
Data centers and industrial loads need high-reliability substations, breakers, protection systems, transformers, and medium-voltage distribution before power becomes usable at the site.

supply_chain_map.node: Large power transformers and distribution transformers
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Transformers are hard-to-substitute electrical hardware with long lead times, limited domestic capacity, import dependence, and demand from utilities, renewables, data centers, manufacturing, and grid hardening.

supply_chain_map.node: Switchgear, breakers, protection relays, and electrical balance-of-plant
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Switchgear and related power-distribution equipment are required at substations and inside mission-critical campuses. Lead-time delays in these lower-cost components can stop an entire data-center or grid project.

supply_chain_map.node: Electrical EPC, specialty contracting, and mission-critical construction labor
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Power-ready campuses require scarce skilled labor, electrical contractors, mechanical contractors, testing, commissioning, and project execution. Labor and EPC capacity can become as binding as equipment supply.

When demand ramps faster than new capacity and interconnection, existing and new gas generation often becomes the marginal source of firm power, especially in ERCOT, PJM, and Southeast load-growth regions.

supply_chain_map.node: Gas turbines and generator step-up equipment
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Hyperscaler, utility, and industrial demand for firm power is colliding with limited gas-turbine manufacturing slots and long power-plant development cycles.

supply_chain_map.node: Natural-gas supply, pipeline deliverability, and storage
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Higher power burn, LNG exports, and winter reliability needs raise the importance of gas availability, pipeline constraints, regional basis spreads, storage adequacy, and fuel-security rules.
Nuclear offers firm, low-carbon power attractive to hyperscalers, but deployment is constrained by licensing, restart economics, construction timelines, fuel-cycle availability, and policy support.

supply_chain_map.node: Nuclear fuel cycle, enrichment, and HALEU
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Advanced reactors and some nuclear expansion scenarios require enriched fuel supply chains that are geopolitically sensitive, technically specialized, and slow to scale.

supply_chain_map.node: Solar, wind, and battery storage additions
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Renewables and batteries are the fastest-to-build capacity in many regions, but they still depend on interconnection, transmission, transformers, permitting, and grid-integration rules.

supply_chain_map.node: Backup power, generators, UPS, batteries, and microgrids
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Mission-critical facilities need backup and on-site power for reliability. If grid access slows, behind-the-meter gas generation, diesel backup, batteries, and microgrids become workaround nodes.

supply_chain_map.node: Copper, electrical steel, GOES, aluminum, and critical grid materials
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Transformers, cables, motors, generators, switchgear, and substations all consume metals and electrical steel. Material tightness can amplify transformer and cable lead-time constraints.

supply_chain_map.node: Capacity markets, rate cases, and cost allocation
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Who pays for new large-load infrastructure affects utility earnings, hyperscaler economics, ratepayer politics, and the pace of approvals. PJM and FERC actions are immediate catalysts.

supply_chain_map.node: Local permitting, water, emissions, and community opposition
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Data centers, gas plants, transmission lines, and substations can be slowed or blocked by local siting, water use, emissions, noise, and ratepayer concerns.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull latest 10-K and quarterly filings to quantify revenue exposure by end market, backlog conversion, book-to-bill, lead times, gross margin sustainability, and whether data-center orders are material versus broader industrial/project-cycle demand.
ticker_relationships.node: Switchgear, medium-voltage distribution, substation control, engineered electrical power distribution
ticker_relationships.relationship: Powell Industries maps directly to the physical power-delivery bottleneck through custom-engineered electrical distribution, control, and switchgear systems used in industrial, utility, and data-center power infrastructure.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track Utility Solutions orders, organic growth, substation-specific acquisitions such as DMC Power, backlog disclosures if available, utility capex commentary, and whether growth is load-driven versus storm/hardening/replacement-driven.
ticker_relationships.node: Utility T&D, substations, grid hardening, electrical solutions
ticker_relationships.relationship: Hubbell maps to front-of-meter utility infrastructure and behind-the-meter electrical products needed for grid expansion, substation work, and electrification; the relationship is strongest where data-center load growth forces utility capex and grid-hardening investment.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Segment backlog by technology/data-center, modular, and electrical operations; verify customer concentration, project margin durability, labor availability, and whether backlog is converting without cost overruns.
ticker_relationships.node: Mission-critical MEP construction, modular construction, electrical contracting, skilled-labor execution
ticker_relationships.relationship: Comfort Systems USA maps to the construction-execution chokepoint because large data-center and advanced-manufacturing loads require scarce mechanical, electrical, plumbing, modular, and skilled-labor capacity before energization.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Quantify data-center percentage of E-Infrastructure revenue, backlog mix, customer concentration, electrical/mechanical acquisition contribution, margin by project type, and sensitivity to warehouse or advanced-manufacturing cyclicality.
ticker_relationships.node: Data-center site development, E-Infrastructure, electrical and mechanical services, pre-interconnection campus work
ticker_relationships.relationship: Sterling Infrastructure maps to the pre-energization infrastructure layer, especially data-center campus site development and E-Infrastructure work that must precede utility interconnection and equipment installation.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track remaining performance obligations/backlog by market sector, acquired versus organic growth after Miller Electric, data-center project margins, labor constraints, and project risk from fixed-price contracts.
ticker_relationships.node: Electrical construction, mechanical construction, network and communications projects, mission-critical facilities
ticker_relationships.relationship: EMCOR maps to mission-critical electrical and mechanical construction capacity, with data centers and network/communications projects creating demand for complex electrical installation, cabling, facilities services, and project execution.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify fiscal 2026 backlog conversion, Communications backlog growth, large-customer concentration, data-center margin sustainability, and whether favorable change orders/scope additions recur.
ticker_relationships.node: Electrical and technology-system installation, communications infrastructure, data-center electrical execution
ticker_relationships.relationship: IES Holdings maps to specialized electrical and technology-system installation capacity, especially through its Communications segment and large data-center projects.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review Dominion's latest IRP, Virginia SCC filings, large-load tariffs, data-center interconnection queue, rate-case outcomes, allowed ROE, cost-allocation rules, and political backlash risk from residential bill impacts.
ticker_relationships.node: Virginia large-load interconnection, regulated utility capex, PJM Dominion zone load growth
ticker_relationships.relationship: Dominion Energy maps to the regulated-utility side of AI/data-center load growth because Northern Virginia data-center demand drives transmission, distribution, generation, and interconnection needs in Dominion Energy Virginia's service territory.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Quantify post-portfolio-shift revenue exposure to data centers and power utilities, growth by vertical, margin contribution, competitive intensity, and whether nVent controls any hard-to-source subcomponent chokepoints.
ticker_relationships.node: Electrical connection and protection, enclosures, data-center infrastructure, power utilities
ticker_relationships.relationship: nVent maps to component-level electrical infrastructure through enclosures, connection/protection products, intelligent power distribution, and data-center/networking solutions used in data-center and utility applications.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Separate contracted hyperscaler PPAs from merchant power exposure; track PJM and ERCOT capacity-market rules, nuclear license extensions, gas repowering execution, hedging levels, fuel costs, emissions policy, and FERC co-location rules.
ticker_relationships.node: Firm dispatchable power, nuclear generation, gas generation, large-load power supply
ticker_relationships.relationship: Vistra maps to firm power scarcity: AI/data-center load growth can increase the value of dispatchable gas and nuclear generation, especially in constrained ERCOT and PJM markets and through long-term hyperscaler power contracts.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track xScale leasing, power availability by market, capex per MW, stabilized yields, PUE, power pass-through mechanics, customer concentration, and whether AI demand improves returns or merely raises power and construction costs.
ticker_relationships.node: Powered data-center capacity, interconnection platform, xScale hyperscale capacity
ticker_relationships.relationship: Equinix maps to the demand-side and platform layer: AI/cloud workloads increase need for powered data-center capacity and interconnection, but the bottleneck relationship depends on Equinix's ability to secure power, land, and customer leases at attractive returns.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track signed-not-opened backlog, MW development pipeline, lease pricing, joint-venture financing, utility power procurement, capex inflation, debt maturity schedule, and whether new AI leases generate adequate risk-adjusted returns.
ticker_relationships.node: Hyperscale data-center capacity, powered shells, AI/cloud leasing, land and power procurement
ticker_relationships.relationship: Digital Realty maps to AI/cloud data-center capacity demand, with power availability and grid interconnection speed acting as constraints on development pipeline conversion.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Quantify Power Systems revenue tied to data centers, generator order backlog, capacity expansion, emissions-compliance risk for diesel backup, competition from Caterpillar/Kohler and batteries, and margin sustainability after strong 2025 demand.
ticker_relationships.node: Backup power, standby generators, prime power, transfer switches, mission-critical reliability
ticker_relationships.relationship: Cummins maps to the data-center reliability layer through standby and prime power generators, controls, paralleling systems, transfer switches, and generator technologies used in mission-critical facilities.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify 2026 quarterly Electrical Americas/Electrical Global backlog, orders, book-to-bill, margin, and percent of orders tied to data centers, utilities, and grid modernization.
ticker_relationships.node: Switchgear, breakers, electrical balance-of-plant, data-center and grid power management
ticker_relationships.relationship: Eaton maps directly to the electrical equipment chokepoint: its 2025 annual report shows Electrical backlog growth, order growth, book-to-bill above 1, and explicit data-center end-market strength. Relationship is broad and high-quality but not pure-play because Eaton also has Aerospace, Vehicle, and eMobility exposure.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check 2026 Electric segment backlog mix, large-load/data-center project exposure, utility versus private customer split, labor availability, and margin sustainability.
ticker_relationships.node: Transmission EPC, distribution EPC, substation construction, large-load center electrical contracting
ticker_relationships.relationship: Quanta maps to the grid-execution bottleneck: it provides electric infrastructure services for electric power, power generation, large load centers, and communications, and reported record 2025 backlog with record Electric segment RPO/backlog. Relationship is close to a labor/execution chokepoint rather than equipment manufacturing.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track 2026 gas turbine order intake, slot reservations, delivery lead times, data-center-linked generation orders, Electrification backlog, and grid factory expansion execution.
ticker_relationships.node: Gas turbines, power generation equipment, grid equipment, high-voltage switchgear, electrification systems
ticker_relationships.relationship: GE Vernova maps to two bottlenecks: dispatchable generation equipment and grid equipment. 2025 disclosures show strong orders, large services backlog, gas-power slot reservation growth, and investment in high-voltage switchgear capacity. Relationship is strong but mixed across Power, Electrification, and Wind.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify NRC restart approvals, project capex, federal/state support, restart timeline, economics of the Microsoft PPA, and whether additional hyperscaler nuclear contracts are signed.
ticker_relationships.node: Firm carbon-free power, nuclear generation, large-load PPAs, PJM data-center power matching
ticker_relationships.relationship: Constellation maps to firm low-carbon power scarcity. Its 20-year Microsoft PPA supports the planned restart of Three Mile Island Unit 1 as the Crane Clean Energy Center and directly links nuclear generation to data-center power matching in PJM.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate 2025/2026 backlog by Government versus Commercial, advanced reactor design and engineering revenue, TRISO/HALEU-related exposure, commercial nuclear component orders, and customer concentration.
ticker_relationships.node: Nuclear components, naval nuclear fuel, commercial nuclear components, advanced reactor design and engineering
ticker_relationships.relationship: BWX Technologies maps to the nuclear supply-chain node through nuclear components, fuel, and services, including government nuclear work and commercial nuclear offerings. Relationship to the AI-power theme is indirect unless advanced reactors, commercial fuel fabrication, or new nuclear projects convert into material orders.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check 2026 DOE task orders, appropriations risk, Piketon/Oak Ridge expansion economics, actual HALEU kg produced, commercial offtake contracts, and NRC licensing milestones.
ticker_relationships.node: Uranium enrichment, HALEU production, advanced reactor fuel-cycle bottleneck
ticker_relationships.relationship: Centrus maps directly to the HALEU chokepoint. DOE has described HALEU as required by most advanced reactor designs, and Centrus has produced nearly one metric ton under DOE-supported work; company filings also disclose DOE HALEU contract amendments and option structures.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track 2026 uranium contracting, realized pricing versus spot/term prices, McArthur River/Cigar Lake output, conversion capacity, Westinghouse order flow, and any direct hyperscaler or reactor-build linkage.
ticker_relationships.node: Uranium supply, UF6 conversion, nuclear fuel services, Westinghouse reactor services
ticker_relationships.relationship: Cameco maps to upstream and midstream nuclear fuel-cycle tightness. Its 2025 annual report discloses uranium production, long-term uranium delivery commitments, record Port Hope UF6 conversion output, about 83 million kgU of contracted UF6 conversion volumes, and Westinghouse earnings exposure.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review CPUC filings, general rate case outcomes, large-load tariffs, wildfire cost recovery, actual data-center interconnection agreements, and ratepayer bill impacts.
ticker_relationships.node: California grid capex, data-center interconnection, regulated transmission and distribution, wildfire hardening
ticker_relationships.relationship: PG&E maps to regulated grid investment and California data-center demand: company sustainability disclosures cite work to serve roughly 10 GW of new data-center demand over the next decade, with 1.4 GW in final design for 2026-2030. Relationship is meaningful but heavily filtered through wildfire liabilities, rate regulation, affordability, and California policy.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate 2026 Georgia/Alabama/Mississippi large-load contracts, IRP generation additions, data-center contracted GW, rate-case recovery, coal/gas/nuclear mix, and customer cost protections.
ticker_relationships.node: Southeast regulated utility load growth, firm generation, nuclear baseload, transmission and distribution capex
ticker_relationships.relationship: Southern maps to the Southeast large-load and firm-power node. The company states projected electric sales growth of 8% annually through 2029, driven by data centers, advanced manufacturing, and residential growth. Relationship is strong at the load-growth level, but economics depend on IRPs, rate cases, generation additions, and cost-allocation rules.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check latest Energy Resources backlog by technology, customer type, data-center exposure, interconnection status, tax-credit sensitivity, equipment procurement, and project COD slippage.
ticker_relationships.node: Renewables, battery storage, contracted clean power for large loads, regulated utility investment
ticker_relationships.relationship: NextEra maps to contracted renewables/storage and utility-scale clean power. 2025 disclosures show Energy Resources adding about 3.2 GW to renewables/storage backlog in Q1 2025 and total backlog around 28 GW after projects placed in service. Serenity relevance depends on whether backlog is interconnection-ready and tied to large-load customers, not generic renewables beta.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify 2026 PPA backlog, data-center customer share, project COD schedule, interconnection status, battery procurement, tax-credit/tariff exposure, and AES Clean Energy margin quality.
ticker_relationships.node: Independent power producer, renewable PPAs, storage, data-center clean-power supply
ticker_relationships.relationship: AES maps to contracted renewables/storage supply for data centers and other large customers. Its 2025 annual report says its Renewables SBU is positioned for data-center growth and identifies solar, wind, storage, and hydro as the Renewables platform. Relationship is plausible but needs project-level PPA and interconnection evidence.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: No evidence needed; maintain one active CEG record for Layer 3.
ticker_relationships.node: Deduplication note
ticker_relationships.relationship: Duplicate CEG candidate was removed from the active relationship universe; retained relationship is the firm carbon-free nuclear PPA mapping above.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify latest contracted capacity, expansion timing at Corpus Christi/Sabine Pass, feedgas sensitivity, spot-vs-contracted margin exposure, and whether data-center-driven U.S. gas demand affects feedgas costs more than LNG export margins.
ticker_relationships.node: LNG exports and global gas supply
ticker_relationships.relationship: Cheniere maps to LNG liquefaction/export capacity and long-term global gas demand rather than direct U.S. data-center power delivery. It can benefit if U.S. gas supply reliability and LNG contract demand remain scarce, but its Serenity chokepoint link is more global and contract-cycle dependent than grid-equipment or behind-the-meter power names.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track contract counterparties, firm-transportation rate economics, project in-service dates, permitting risk, capex-to-EBITDA conversion, and whether new gas demand is incremental or displaces other volumes.
ticker_relationships.node: Natural-gas transportation, storage, and data-center/power-plant laterals
ticker_relationships.relationship: Energy Transfer has a direct relationship to gas-fired power and data-center load through natural-gas pipeline capacity, storage, and announced projects serving power plants and data-center sites. The relationship is stronger than generic midstream because recent disclosures reference contracted demand-pull capacity and specific data-center/power customers.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate NEO and Atlas economics, customer credit quality, regulatory approvals, turbine/generator procurement, gas supply availability, and whether behind-the-meter offerings create higher-return infrastructure revenue or only incremental pipeline throughput.
ticker_relationships.node: Natural-gas transmission, data-center behind-the-meter power, and pipeline constraints
ticker_relationships.relationship: Williams maps directly to gas infrastructure for AI/data-center power demand through Transco-linked expansions, behind-the-meter generation concepts, and specific data-center capacity agreements. Within this chunk, WMB has one of the clearest company-level links to the data-center power chokepoint.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check Creekside and other lateral projects, data-center/customer contracts, regional overlap with ERCOT/Southeast/PJM large-load growth, tariff terms, and new capacity vs. existing capacity utilization.
ticker_relationships.node: Natural-gas pipeline network and power-generation demand
ticker_relationships.relationship: Kinder Morgan maps to gas transport for LNG feedgas, industrial demand, and gas-fired power needs, with management materials positioning the network for surging data-center power demand. Relationship is credible but requires specific regional project/customer validation to separate chokepoint exposure from broad gas-pipeline beta.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track new bookings velocity, ASPs for 2029+ deliveries, utilization at U.S. vs. international plants, Section 45X/FEOC/Section 232 outcomes, cancellation clauses, and backlog margin conversion.
ticker_relationships.node: Domestic utility-scale solar module manufacturing
ticker_relationships.relationship: First Solar maps to domestic renewable generation supply and U.S. manufacturing scarcity, with a large contracted backlog and policy/tariff-linked domestic-content angle. Serenity relevance is moderate because solar generation still depends on interconnection, transmission, storage, and firming; its bottleneck is more domestic module availability and policy durability than immediate dispatchable power.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify channel inventory normalization, battery attach rates, VPP/utility program revenue, commercial product traction, U.S. vs. Europe recovery, tariff/45X effects, and whether grid-edge software becomes material to revenue.
ticker_relationships.node: Residential solar microinverters, batteries, and grid-edge energy management
ticker_relationships.relationship: Enphase maps to distributed energy and residential grid-edge flexibility rather than utility-scale AI power delivery. Current evidence shows weak U.S. residential demand after tax-credit expiration, so the Serenity relationship should remain lower priority unless batteries, virtual power plants, or commercial/grid-edge products show durable demand independent of residential solar cyclicality.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track backlog conversion to revenue/gross margin, order intake, domestic content/IRA exposure, battery-cell supply, customer concentration, grid-forming controls adoption, warranty provisions, and cash-flow quality.
ticker_relationships.node: Grid-scale battery storage, grid flexibility, and renewables integration
ticker_relationships.relationship: Fluence maps to grid-scale storage systems and software, a potential flexibility chokepoint as data-center load and renewables strain transmission and capacity markets. The relationship is meaningful, but backlog profitability, component sourcing, competition, and interconnection timing remain key validation items.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check current copper supply-demand balance, treatment/refining charges, Grasberg/Indonesia risk, U.S. copper policy, unit cash costs, production growth, and sensitivity to copper price vs. gold/moly byproducts.
ticker_relationships.node: Copper supply for grid expansion, electrification, data centers, and industrial infrastructure
ticker_relationships.relationship: Freeport-McMoRan maps to copper as an upstream material pulled by grid buildout, electrical equipment, data centers, and electrification. Serenity relevance is real but indirect: copper is a broad commodity exposure, so thesis quality depends on copper price, mine supply, jurisdictional risk, and cost curve rather than only AI power demand.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate 2026 production/capex guidance, project pipeline in Peru/Mexico, permitting/community risk, unit costs, dividend policy, reserve life, and realized copper price leverage.
ticker_relationships.node: Copper supply for energy transition and grid materials
ticker_relationships.relationship: Southern Copper maps to copper demand from energy transition, grid investment, and electrification. The relationship is broad and commodity-linked; Serenity relevance depends on whether SCCO offers differentiated production growth, cost advantage, or scarcity exposure relative to other copper producers.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track magnetics ramp, DoD contract terms, heavy rare earth sourcing, NdPr pricing, customer/offtake volumes, China dependency reduction, separation yields, and whether energy-transition end markets become material revenue drivers.
ticker_relationships.node: Rare earth mining, separation, and U.S. magnet supply chain
ticker_relationships.relationship: MP Materials maps to critical minerals and magnet supply chains used in motors, defense, robotics, wind, and electrification. It is strategically relevant to energy and industrial electrification but less direct to the immediate AI data-center power bottleneck than gas pipelines, transformers, switchgear, and grid-scale storage.
